manifest.name: dsh-max-compact
manifest.description: Compact model input for DeepSeek Harness (>= 0.2): a lazy tool surface that hides tool definitions behind an on-demand discover tool (dsh-ops style, but for every plugin's tools), a deployment-level prompt layer (trailing sections, editable persona, prompt files/profiles), and a preset composer that clones and toggles agent-preset rows through the agentPresets registry.

bundle.text:
# dsh-max-compact profile bundle (DSH >= 0.2).
#
# Single global row `max-compact` mounts at profile scope — intentionally NOT
# inside a preset — so the lazy-tool surface, prompt layer, persona shadow and
# /mc commands apply to every agent and every preset (including foreign ones).
# All behavior is config-gated: the one default-active piece is ponytail's
# `lite` baseline (opt out via `ponytailDefault: off` or `/mc pt default off`).
- insert:
    - id: max-compact
      name: dsh-max-compact
      config: {}

declared.name: prompt set Keep answers under 100 lines.
section set app:web-surface GUI only; never start a server.
section trim tier-routing Tiered session guard smart Never
section set app:web-surface slim GUI text

readme.text:
Compact model input for DeepSeek Harness (DSH >= 0.2): shrink what the model
sees — tool definitions, prompt sections, preset compositions — without
shrinking what the deployment can do.

Five mechanisms, one plugin — all config-gated (ponytail ships an opt-out
`lite` default; everything else is inert until configured):

1. **Lazy tool surface.** Most tools hide behind `mc_discover`: the model sees
   a small resident surface (fs + shell + messaging) and activates anything
   else on demand — the dsh-ops discovery pattern, generalized to *every*
   plugin's tools, not just one catalog.
2. **Editable prompt layer + persona shadow.** A trailing system-prompt
   section the deployment owns — inline text, an external `prompt.md`-style
   file (re-read every step, mtime-cached), or named profiles — plus a
   per-agent `deployment:persona-prefix` override that shadows whatever the
   preset's persona row declared, without touching the preset.
3. **Preset composer.** `agentPresets.list()` shows the whole roster —
   official, foreign, managed. `readDocument` + `register` clone any preset
   under a new id with per-row `disabled` toggles (the dsh-custom-mode
   capability, but for *all* presets, since foreign declarations are
   read-only but clonable).
4. **Managed prompt sections.** `/mc section` pins hide/shadow/trim rules to
   named prompt sections, scoped per agent (`all` | `subagents` | preset
   ids); the assemble waterfall applies them every step, independent of the
   lazy switch.
5. **Ponytail m

Everything is capability-probed: a missing seam disables the feature with an
honest `/mc status` line, never a crash.

```sh
npm install dsh-max-compact
npm install github:20genesis14-sys/dsh-max-compact

readme.section: or add the plugin directory to the profile's plugin list
readme.text:
```

The bundle mounts one global row (`id: max-compact`) — intentionally *not*
inside a preset, so every mechanism covers every agent and every preset,
including foreign ones. With the default config only ponytail's `lite`
baseline is active (everything else is inert); `ponytailDefault: off` or
`/mc pt default off` silences it too.

```
/mc                                    # status: seams, lazy stats, layer, persona, presets
/mc lazy on|off                        # enable/disable the compact surface
/mc lazy keep|hide|default <tool>      # adjust the resident/lazy policy
/mc lazy release <tool> | reset        # re-mask activated tool(s) on this session

`/mc` output also lands on an expanded transcript card plus a floating result
panel (the bundled `client/` web half), so it stays visible on a fresh
session's hero screen.

Bundled skills (`skills/` dir, vendored MIT from `@wenaixi/dsh-ponytail`):
`ponytail-review` (diff review for over-engineering), `ponytail-audit`
(whole-repo), `ponytail-debt` (`ponytail:`-marker ledger). The model calls
the `skill` tool by name, or you invoke a skill directly.

`stop ponytail` or `normal mode` as a whole message also flips the session off.

In-session the model gets `mc_discover`:

```
mc_discover({query: "web"})  ->  "Selected web_search, web_fetch. They become
callable on the next model step; nothing was executed."
```

- `agent.ctx.tools.register` puts `mc_discover` in the agent's **own layer** —
  restrictions never cover own-layer registrations, so the activation path
  can never mask itself. Its disposer lives in `ownLifts`, separate from the
  restrict masks that `reconcile` lifts on every recompute.
- `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({deny})` masks the lazy set per agent. Reconcile
  follows the official-tool-hiding discipline: a public-surface snapshot
  diff guards against publication feedback loops, all masks lift before
  recompute, a failed plan hides nothing, and `deny` narrows on scope-local
  or unknown names (`restrict` throws naming the offender — that tool is
  honestly reported as unmaskable rather than silently kept).
- Activations queue into `pending` and commit at the next step boundary
  (`agent/pre-step`, `session/event` `step/end` as fallback) — republishing
  mid-step would invalidate the in-flight request's tool list. Activated
  tools stay visible for the agent's lifetime (`/mc lazy release <tool>` or
  `reset` re-masks them).
- A **global** `ctx.tools.guard(exec => …)` keyed on `exec.agent` denies
  hidden-tool executions even from conversation history; activation lifts
  the

One global `system-prompt/assemble` listener (`context.scope` = the
assembling agent) drops sections that document currently-masked tools —
`tools:workflow` and friends stop burning tokens while their tool is lazy.
The waterfall cannot rewrite a `complete` section (the host restores it);
that limit is documented, not worked around. `/mc sections` inspects the
last assembly.

- **hide** — the waterfall drops the section for matching agents. The only
  mode that works on *agent-scoped* contributions (shadows would collide in
  the same layer).
- **shadow** — same-name section registered in the agent's own scope
  replaces the original (deeper layer wins by name, the host's own persona
  mechanism). Order self-heals: the waterfall records the original's
  position and the shadow re-registers there once seen.
- **trim** — lines containing a keep-substring survive; the only mode safe
  for *dynamic* sections (`tier-routing` shows live tier labels — a static
  shadow would freeze stale values, so `set` refuses the `NO_SHADOW` list).

Scopes follow `matchesScope`: `all` (default) | `subagents` | preset ids.
Agents without `session.meta` (older hosts) match only `all`. Multiple
rules may target the same name — hide wins over shadow for a matching
agent, so "shadow for all + hide for subagents" compresses parents and
drops the section for children. A `trim` whose patterns match nothing
leaves the original text — a mistyped rule must degrade to "unchanged",
never to "silently deleted". Rules persist in the settings document and
lift instantly on `/mc section off`.

Section `maxcompact:layer` (order 10500, after `deployment:persona-prefix`
and suffix) resolves each assembly: file > active profile > inline. Files
are re-read every step through an mtime/size cache — external edits land on
the next model call with no reload.

`deployment:persona-prefix` (order 0) registered in the agent's **own**
scope shadows the preset's persona row — same-name sections shadow across
layers (duplicate names only collide *within* one layer). Off by default;
`/mc persona set`/`off` refreshes every live agent.

One global `maxcompact:ponytail` section (order 50) renders ONLY the baseline
locked at `agent/created` — mid-session `/mc pt` switches never re-hash the
prompt prefix. Mode changes travel as one tagged `<system-reminder>` user
message appended on the `agent/pre-step` waterfall (a retry replaces it by
tag). `stop ponytail` / `normal mode` as a whole message flips the session
off. Default resolution: `PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE` env → `ponytailDefault`
field → `lite`. The vendored `skills/` catalog registers through
`skills.registerProvider`; `maxcompact:ponytail` is denylisted from managed
sections (`NO_MANAGE`).

- `agentPresets.list()` — every declared preset incl. `broken` diagnostics.
- `readDocument(id)` — the full composition YAML, parsed with a `!!js` →
  `{__jsExpr}` schema so host-evaluated predicates survive cloning verbatim.
- Clone registers under a **new** id (foreign declarations are never
  touched); `group`/`isolate` structure is preserved so service rows keep
  their realms; relative `./x.mjs` specifiers become absolute `file://` URLs.
- Toggle = `disabled: true` on the row + dispose/re-register (duplicate ids
  throw — disposal first). **New sessions pick up the new revision; running
  sessions keep their retained generation.** That's the platform's
  revision-retention design, not a limitation of this plugin.
- Managed specs persist through the volatile `managedPresets` field and the
  settings document (ns `max-compact`) — clones survive restarts.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lazyEnabled` | `false` | Master switch for the compact surface |
| `lazyKeep` | `[]` | Extra tool names to keep resident |
| `lazyHide` | `[]` | Tool names forced lazy (beats keep) |
| `lazyHideSections` | `[]` | Section names filtered from assemblies while lazy is on |
| `customPrompt` | `''` | Inline layer text |
| `customPromptFile` | `''` | External prompt file path |
| `promptProfiles` | `{}` | `{name: text}` named layers |
| `activePromptProfile` | `''` | Selected profile |
| `customPersona` | `''` | Persona shadow text |
| `layerPresets` | `[]` | Layer scope: `[]` all, `[':subagent']` delegates only, preset ids |
| `personaPresets` | `[]` | Persona scope, same vocabulary |
| `managedSections` | `[]` | `[{name, mode, text?, keep?, scope?}]` hide/shadow/trim rules; several rules may target one name under different scopes (hide wins over shadow) |
| `managedPresets` | `[]` | Cloned preset specs |
| `ponytailDefault` | unset | Ponytail baseline for new sessions — `PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE` env wins; falls back to `lite` |

- **Preview APIs.** `agentPresets`, `tools.restrict`/`guard`,
  `system-prompt/assemble` are preview surfaces — all probed; missing seams
  degrade features, never crash.
- **Global rows can still add tools.** Profile-global plugins mount on top
  of any preset — no preset or mask fences *their* own-layer additions, so
  `/mc lazy list` reports what the host actually shows, not an ideal count.
- **Foreign presets are read-only.** `readDocument` is "for viewing only" —
  clone under a new id to customize; the original is never edited in place.
- **`complete` sections can't be rewritten** by the assemble waterfall —
  including a `complete` persona. The persona shadow uses a named prefix
  section instead, which layering *does* shadow.
- **Shadows freeze static text.** Sections resolving live state per step
  (`tier-routing`'s tier labels) belong to `trim`, not `set` — the
  `NO_SHADOW` denylist enforces it. Agent-scoped contributions (registered
  per-agent by the host, e.g. `context:file-reference`) collide with a
  shadow in the same layer — use `hide` for those.
- **Revision retention.** Preset toggles affect new sessions; running
  sessions keep the generation they mounted.

```sh
npm test           # 88 tests — pure core + mocked-ctx smoke
npm run check      # node --check every lib file
npm run pack:check # npm pack --dry-run
```

`lib/core/` is pure logic (no DSH imports, no I/O); `lib/dsh/` is the only
place that knows DSH exists; `lib/index.js` wires the two. Per-agent state
lives in `WeakMap`s keyed on agent objects — never session-id strings.
